extracted.intended_audience: people seeking beginner (and entry-level) improv classes / adult students interested in improv
extracted.subtask_description: A beginning-level, in-person improv course teaching fundamentals through warm-ups, games, scene work, and simple monologues; aimed at newcomers and those with some prior improv experience to build confidence, speaking skills, and spontaneity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fun warm ups and games
rubrics_metrics.description: From day one you will jump into a series of fun warm ups and games designed to ease you into improv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early-class activities intended to acclimate students to improvisation; emphasis on active participation and gradual introduction to improv practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Playing scenes
rubrics_metrics.description: Before you know it you will be playing scenes...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students will practice scene work as a core activity of the class; progression from exercises to enacted scenes is expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heighten and explore ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn how to heighten and explore your ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on developing and amplifying ideas within scenes (the page emphasizes learning the skill of heightening and idea exploration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-person scenes
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn how to do 2 person scenes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Skill development specifically for paired scene work and partnering dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group scenes
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn how to do group scenes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training in ensemble scene work and managing multi-person interactions onstage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group games
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation in structured group improv games as a method to build skills, spontaneity, and group dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliver simple monologues
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn how to deliver simple monologues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice giving short solo pieces to develop presence and narrative confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong fundamentals
rubrics_metrics.description: You will learn strong fundamentals that will build your confidence, improve speaking skills and foster spontaneity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course emphasis is on foundational improv techniques and principles that underpin later work; these fundamentals are presented as the primary learning goal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build confidence
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An explicit learning outcome: the class aims to increase students' confidence through practice and supportive environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve speaking skills
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An explicit outcome: practicing scene work, monologues, and games is intended to enhance students' verbal expression and communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foster spontaneity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The curriculum targets increased spontaneity as a measurable outcome of improv exercises and scene practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fun and supportive environment
rubrics_metrics.description: The class is all about fun and support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pedagogical tone: exercises and feedback are framed to be encouraging and enjoyable rather than high-pressure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitable for beginners and those with experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether you are a beginner who has never improvised or someone who has improv experience, you will learn strong fundamentals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course is accessible to total beginners while still offering foundational skill-building for students with some prior experience.
